title: Multiorgan Photon Counting CT and Machine Learning to Elucidate Aging Mechanisms and Interventions
text:
This project investigates how liver health influences systemic aging across the heart, brain, and bone in
genetically engineered APOE mouse models. Using advanced photon-counting CT imaging, AI–based
multiorgan aging clocks, and molecular profiling, we will test whether early hepatic changes, such as altered
fat, iron, perfusion, and cytokine signaling drive age-related decline in other organs. This integrative approach
will reveal modifiable liver-centered pathways of aging, identify imaging-based biomarkers of systemic decline,
and inform precision interventions for age-related diseases including Alzheimer’s, cardiovascular disease, and
osteoporosis.

title: The Intermountain West-Atlantic Center (InterACT) for the APS Phenotyping Consortium
text:
The Intermountain West-Atlantic Center (InterACT) brings together four technically experienced, high-enrolling
sites to participate in the APS Phenotypes Consortium. InterACT will use robust statistical methods to
phenotype patients with Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS), pneumonia, and sepsis in two broad
proposals that incorporate target trial emulation to confirm phenotypes. The Consortium-wide proposal focuses
on clinical data and inflammatory cytokines, while the Center-specific proposal investigates hyaluronan and
tissue injury and repair pathways.

title: Personalized Deep Brain Stimulation for Epilepsy
text:
PROJECT NARATIVE
Epilepsy affects 1% of the U.S. population, with a third facing drug-resistant forms; while thalamic deep brain
stimulation and other neuromodulation therapies are FDA-approved, they seldom achieve complete seizure
control, and are limited by a generic approach. We posit that seizure control can be significantly enhanced by a
personalized neuromodulation strategy that involves seizure network (SN)-specific electrode placement and
the use of short-latency biomarkers for data-driven assessments of stimulation effects. This proposal employs
stereotactic EEG with thalamic electrodes and brain stimulation techniques to map, characterize, and modulate
brain networks, to advance a highly personalized approach to electrode placement and parameter optimization
for epilepsy neuromodulation.

title: A Randomized Controlled Trial of Prophylaxis with Direct-acting Antivirals for Kidney Transplantation from Hepatitis C virus-infected donor to Uninfected Recipients (PREVENT-HCV)
text:
Due to epidemics of opioid overdose and hepatitis C virus (HCV), organs from HCV+ donors are increasingly
available, however thousands are currently discarded that could benefit individuals in need of a transplant. A
new practice of transplanting HCV+ donor organs into individuals without HCV, in combination with HCV
medications, has shown early success. This proposal includes a trial of HCV+ donor kidney transplantation in
order to determine the best timing and duration of HCV medications, and scientific studies that will improve our
understanding of HCV infection and immune responses, as well as novel viruses.

title: Developing A Diverse Workforce: Advancing Data Science for Addiction Research and Professional Training (ADAPT)
text:
This proposal is relevant to public health because it works to unlock the complex intersection of addiction and
big data for a more diverse workforce. Creating curated and scalable training for a broad audience of trainees
can enhance our ability to solve problems in addiction science. This research aligns with NIH NIDA's goal to
provide the highest quality research training to a diverse workforce.

title: Investigating the lasting effects of adolescent cannabinoid exposure on mesocortical development
text:
Exposure to cannabis and cannabinoids during adolescence may have a long-lasting effect on executive
function. The proposed research project will investigate the protracted impact of exposure to Δ-9-
tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) on the development of neurotransmitter systems within key brain regions that
support cognitive function. The results of these studies will contribute to our understanding of how cannabinoid
exposure during a vulnerable period can influence neuronal development and executive function.

title: Collaboration on HIV and AgingResearch through the Study of Mitochondria
text:
NARRATIVE/RELEVANCE
The lifespan of people with HIV has been considerably extended, but the burden of age-related comorbidities
remains high among them. This proposal will evaluate the role of mitochondrial function and DNA methylation
in biological aging (represented by frailty phenotypes, epigenetic clock acceleration, and immunosenescence)
among people with HIV, as well evaluate the potential of exercise to reverse mitochondrial function damage
and epigenetic clock acceleration caused by HIV. Completion of this proposal will enhance the understanding
of the role of mitochondrial function in age acceleration among people with HIV as well as highlight potential
interventions to mitigate the damage, which ultimately could lead to improvements in treatment and long-term
care strategies for people aging with HIV.

title: Skin Stem Cells and Their Niche Interactions
text:
Stem cells (SCs) are natural units of tissue repair and homeostasis, and their versatility holds promise for tissue
regeneration. This research uses the skin epithelium as a model to delineate the crosstalk that SCs undergo
with their local microenvironments which enable SCs to self-renew and survive long-term during normal tissue
homeostasis and in response to injuries. Understanding how SCs cope with stress and with breaches in the
epithelial barrier is a fundamental prerequisite to ascertaining the potential of SCs for regenerative therapies and
to devise new and improved therapeutics for inflammatory disorders and cancers.

title: COPD GWAS Functional Variant Identification in Airway Epithelial Cells using Deep Learning Splicing Models
text:
Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is one of the leading causes of
mortality, but we have not yet discovered treatments that significantly reverse the lung damage of COPD. In
this project, we will study an important cell type for COPD, human airway epithelial cells (HAECs), and we will
understand how genetic differences between individuals can increase risk for COPD by their effects on
alternative splicing in HAECs. We will use advanced long read sequencing and proteomic technologies, as
well as deep learning models of alternative splicing to identify how COPD-causing genetic differences that
affect splicing have broader effects on the biological processes and cellular functions of HAECs.

title: The role of positive emotions in stress-induced negative emotion regulation among older adults with mild cognitive impairment
text:
Although positive affect has been widely recognized for its role in buffering against negative emotions among
cognitively healthy individuals, it remains unclear whether this benefit extends to older adults with mild cognitive
impairment (MCI)—a population particularly vulnerable to high stress and negative emotions, which increase
their risk of progressing to dementia. This study aims to address this significant gap by exploring the role of
positive emotions in regulating stress-induced negative emotions in both controlled laboratory and everyday
settings for older adults with MCI. Enhancing our understanding of how positive emotions affect emotion
regulation could potentially inform the development of innovative, targeted interventions that might delay or even
prevent the progression of dementia in this at-risk population.

title: Investigating the role of cell cycle plasticity in the growth and progression of bladder cancers
text:
Cancer cells need to divide and multiply to form tumors, but we have only recently discovered
that they can take different "paths" to do this, a phenomenon known as cell cycle plasticity. These
growth patterns seem to be influenced by neighboring cells, such as immune and support cells,
though we don't yet fully understand which ones are most important or how they affect cancer cell
division. This study will use cutting-edge imaging technology to analyze hundreds of bladder
cancer samples from patient donors, mapping out these growth paths and shedding light on how
the tumor’s cellular environment impacts cancer cell division. This could lead to new treatments
for bladder cancer by targeting both the growth patterns of cancer cells and their influential
neighbors.

title: Development of novel epigenetic biomarkers and detection reagents for aging
text:
Aging and neurodegenerative diseases, such as Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias are
associated with deterioration of chromatin structure. Chromatin structure is informed by combinatorial
chromatin features, which can be informative biomarkers but are difficult or impossible to study without
complex proteomics methods. Here, EpiCypher is developing a pipeline for the unbiased discovery of aging-
associated combinatorial marks and development of cognate detection reagents to identify and validate novel
biomarkers and therapeutic targets of aging and age-related diseases.

title: Comparative Modeling of Multiple Myeloma Prevention, Early Detection and Treatment Interventions
text:
RELEVANCE: Multiple myeloma (MM) is a common, incurable hematologic cancer with an extremely high
health and economic burden, necessitating a coordinated and concerted effort to advance prevention and
control strategies. The CISNET MM Working Group aims to expand three existing CISNET-standard natural
history models to study incidence trends, evaluate novel management strategies for MM and smoldering MM
(SMM), and improve care accessibility and affordability. The proposed U01 initiative leverages MMWG's
unique expertise and robust data to address critical questions, assess interventions, and inform policy
decisions in MM and SMM management with the goal of improving patient outcomes and reducing the burden
of MM.

title: Develop a novel red blood cell-based microfluidic approach to assess and diagnose ME/CFS
text:
Identifying new laboratory tests that can measure the progression of ME/CFS will directly improve
the diagnosis and treatment of ME/CFS and contribute to our understanding of mechanisms
underlying ME/CFS. This research develops an interdisciplinary approach to assess the recently
discovered, oxygen tension-regulated red blood cell capillary velocity as a new laboratory test for
ME/CFS and investigate previously unrealized red blood cell cytokine signaling in ME/CFS.
Because ME/CFS is a poorly understood, complex, debilitating disease with no specific laboratory
diagnostic tests yet, we believe the proposed project is directly relevant to the NIH's mission and
should be broadly valuable for research efforts and clinical studies of chronic diseases including
recently emerged long COVID.

title: Developing a Double Saturation Technique to Enhance CEST Quantification at 3T and Its Application in Muscle Glycogen Imaging
text:
The proposed research holds significant relevance to public health as it aims to develop an innovative
glycogen imaging method at clinical MRI scanners that holds promising potential for routine clinical application.
The proposed research is relevant to NIBIB mission to improve health by leading the development of imaging
technologies.

title: Multiplex binding antibody assay for confirmatory HSV-1/2 serological diagnosis
text:
This proposal aims to develop and clinically validate a precise, convenient and scalable serology test for Herpes
Simplex Virus type 1 and 2. The overall goal of the project is to replace currently used ineffective and laborious
two-step HSV testing by a high-throughput, one-step assay with high specificity and sensitivity in differentiation
of HSV type. This new test can be run both in central labs and can be kitted and licensed for future regulatory
submissions that would allow it to be run in hundreds of clinical laboratories around the United States and world.

title: Endothelial plasticity in glioma vascularization and therapy resistance
text:
Glioblastoma (GBM) is among the most lethal of human malignancies with a current median
survival of about 14 months. The goals of this project are to understand the mechanism of tumor
therapy resistance and to develop new therapy for treating GBM.

title: Development of High-Speed Atomic Force Microscope-Infrared Microscopy in the Aqueous Phase
text: This technology development project aims to create a high-speed atomic force microscopy-infrared (HS-AFM- IR) imaging tool that provides real-time, label-free, and chemically sensitive visualization of the dynamics of biomacromolecules in aqueous environments. This technology will enable scientists to observe critical molecular interactions, such as protein self-assembly and antibody-antigen interaction, with high spatial resolution and chemical sensitivity. The development of this tool will advance biomedical research and therapeutic development, ultimately enhancing public health by facilitating the discovery of new treatments for diseases through controlling biomacromolecule interactions.

title: Uncovering Heterogeneity in Individual Treatment Responses via Causal Machine Learning
text:
This research will answer key questions about predictors for heterogeneity of individual treatment responses
and alleviate the problem of robustness of prediction models across populations. Our results will shed light on
the markers leading to individual variations in treatment responses, enable better risk assessment, and
ultimately provide the key to personalized medicine.

title: BIOME Core
text: Since 2016, the Nebraska Center for Integrated Biomolecular Communication (NCIBC) has established itself as a leader in advanced biomedical research by integrating cutting-edge microscopy, OMICS, and structural biology technologies. In Phases 1 and 2, NCIBC developed two core facilities, the Systems Biology Core (SBC) and Light and Electron Microscopy Core (LEMC), which collectively provided comprehensive services including high- quality microscopy imaging, cryo-electron microscopy, mass spectrometry-based metabolomics, lipidomics, proteomics, nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) metabolomics, and ligand affinity screening. This success was made possible by uniting four long-standing, financially self-sustaining facilities at the University of Nebraska- Lincoln, thereby creating robust infrastructure for sample and data management, expanding instrumentation, software, and experimental protocols, and supporting a broad user base of over 120 research groups and 500 grant proposals. Building on this strong foundation, Phase 3 aims to unify SBC and LEMC into a single entity, the Biomolecular Imaging, Omics, and Molecular Exploration (BIOME) Core. This consolidation seeks to enhance operational efficiency and financial sustainability while maintaining the range of state-of-the-art services available to both academic and industrial researchers. BIOME’s distinct value lies in its collaborative, hands-on approach, providing expert guidance throughout the research lifecycle, from experimental design and sample preparation to data analysis and dissemination, thereby maximizing the impact and quality of complex OMICS, microscopy, and structural biology studies. Phase 3 goals focus on broadening BIOME’s user base through outreach and training, meeting institutional benchmarks to secure long-term funding, and integrating automation and artificial intelligence to optimize workflows and improve data quality. Expected outcomes include expanded services, increased throughput and efficiency, enhanced training opportunities for non-expert users, and sustainable growth that ensures BIOME remains a vital resource for the NCIBC and the wider research community well into the future.
